This study reports improving task-completion capability in a bounded software evaluation. Its narrower task distribution cannot establish generality across arbitrary domains; the availability date identifies the version read.

The study challenges the assumption that increasing model capability automatically improves reliability. Its findings concern particular models and reliability tests, so they do not disprove Marcus's broader long-run forecast.
